strategy: Authoritative qualitative route semantics, official habitat context, route-specific seasonal evidence and conservative carry-water policy

newlySupported.result: The approved circuit stays at 2,283–2,454 m; official park habitat guidance places Alpine meadows above the timber line. ORMA therefore uses the conservative non-quantified instruction that dependable tree shade should not be expected.

The official full-circuit description identifies a wide outward path and a narrower but unchallenging return, while the technical sheet supplies gravel, stone, drainage-channel, width and exposure detail for the outbound segment. No whole-route dog rating is inferred.
A current official destination guide describes flowered pasture and audible cowbells beside the Lavaredo segment. Seasonal presence remains variable and guardian dogs are not established.
The operator's turn-by-turn itinerary directly supports an exposed upper panoramic/refuge zone followed by a forest return. No shade percentage is assigned.
The current circuit narrative directly identifies tree/forest portions and open southern beaches/lakeshore. No shade percentage is assigned.
No official source reviewed identifies a potable route fountain. The publishable safety instruction is to carry all dog water and never treat the protected lake as a verified source.

guardrails: Qualitative shade statements are deliberately not converted into canopy percentages.
Absence of a verified fountain is not presented as proof that no water service exists; it triggers a carry-all-water instruction.
Seasonal livestock evidence never implies a guaranteed encounter or guardian-dog presence.
All six resolutions remain proposals until the human safety-input gate confirms their exact wording.
